title: Tzur Mishelo
description: Tzur Mishelo, a Sabbath table song, in Hebrew to a German melody printed in 1906, for 2 to 4 singers. The refrain calls the faithful to bless the Rock whose food we have eaten: we have eaten our fill and left over, as Hashem promised. Verse 1 thanks the One who feeds the world, our shepherd and father, and verse 4 asks for the Temple to be rebuilt, with a new song and a full cup of wine.

credits.words: traditional Hebrew Sabbath table hymn (zemer), anonymous

licence.source: melody from The Jewish Encyclopedia, vol. 12 (New York and London: Funk and Wagnalls, 1906), article "Zemirot" by Joseph Jacobs and Francis L. Cohen (Jacobs died 1916, Cohen 1934), p. 658, the example headed "SABBATH REST", Lento, 6/8, two flats in the signature, in G minor (it ends on G, with F-sharp leading notes), 16 bars and a pickup, printed with three English verses ("This day is to our race Of all seasons the best"); the article names it "a German melody employed either with the 'Yom Zeh le-Yisrael' of Isaac Luria or with the anonymous 'Zur mi-Shello Akalnu'". Written here in G minor as printed; the tune's top F5 (twice, in verse bars 10) is a semitone over the soprano range. The Hebrew is fitted by us in modern Israeli pronunciation: the refrain to the first eight bars ("Tzur mishelo achalnu"), the verses to all sixteen (verse 1, "Hazan et olamo", and verse 4, "Yibane hamikdash"), the refrain sung first, between the verses and last. Each half-line of the hymn takes one two-bar phrase; where a line has more syllables the printed dotted quarter and quarter under one slur are sung as two syllables, and where it has fewer two notes share one (the print's slur kept at "kos"). Divine names in the substituted form sung outside prayer: "Adoshem" (and "kadoshem") for the four-letter name, on the same notes. Breaths written in for beginners: at the end of bars 4 and 12 the slurred quarter is sung as an eighth and the next pickup starts a sixth of a beat late; at bars 8 and 16 the long G gives up half a beat. Read from the scan at storage.googleapis.com/jewishencyclopedia/images/V12p658001.jpg (jewishencyclopedia.com, "ZEMIROT").
